entries.title: Herbs can interact with medicines
entries.content: Herbal supplements can interact with prescription drugs; for example St. John's wort can make some birth control and other medicines work less well. Always ask a doctor or pharmacist first.
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Supplements aren't pre-approved
entries.content: In the US, dietary supplements don't need FDA approval for safety or effectiveness before sale. Quality and strength can vary between products.
entries.source: Herbal Supplements: Quality and Safety Concerns
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Probiotics basics
entries.content: Probiotics are live microbes found in some foods and supplements; effects depend on the specific strain. NCCIH warns they can be risky for premature infants and people with weak immune systems.
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only
